title: Favorite trombonists
summary: Asked for favorite trombonists, Desvigne names Vic Gaspard, Buddy Johnson, Benirap and Louis Nelson, who played well when sober.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Speaking of trombone, I wonder if you could talk just for a minute or two about trombone players. Who was your favorite trombone player? You mentioned much George Field, but of all the different trombonists you've heard or worked with, who were some of the greatest that you remember? The best ones, or your favorites, you might say. Either people that worked with you or others that you heard when you were a kid?

I didn't know too many trombone players. I know the names of Vic Gasper and Buddy Johnson. You know Benirap? I never did know that guy, Benirap. I mean, he was a great trombone player, but I didn't know him.
I didn't know that guy. I never knew he'd die.
I never knew he'd die. What about you?
Louis Nelson was the only one that Louis Nelson could play very good trombone when he didn't drink. Yeah, that's right.
